Digital overgrowth is the most consistent feature of activating NPR2 alleles, but why the great toe is preferentially enlarged is unknown. A role for cGMP-mediated inhibition of PDE3A in digit formation has been proposed and is untested.
The enlarged great toe is wide as well as long; the intervening steps are not characterized.
Overgrowth of the phalanges lengthens the fingers and toes, as seen in the mouse model; the human step is inferred.

nodes.description: Activating NPR2 alleles hold the receptor in a conformation that mimics the allosterically (ATP-) activated state. Depending on the allele, basal maximal velocity rises, the Km for GTP and EC50 for CNP fall, the requirement for ATP or receptor phosphorylation changes, and normal desensitization is lost. The guanylyl cyclase is therefore driven outside its normal ligand and phosphorylation control, which is why the activity is annotated as gain of function rather than a quantitative increase. The ATP analogue TNP-ATP inhibits the mutant but not the wild-type receptor in vitro, an experimental lead with no clinical data.
